subtype: Online group × Being trolled or shamed [Receiver]
passage: The night before his thermodynamics exam, Joseph's post about a film had gone the wrong way. Strangers mocked his accent, called him names, and their comments were still arriving. His hands shook over the keyboard. He typed a long reply, and Reena, from the next bunk, looked over. "Don't send that." "They're lying about me!" "They'll only get more to pile on." She showed him how to screenshot the worst messages, block the accounts, and switch off notifications until tomorrow. Joseph felt hot behind his eyes. "It hurts, though." "I know. It says nothing true about you." She made two cups of tea, and they went through his formulas until midnight. In the morning, he still felt bruised, but he walked into the exam.

qa.q: What did Reena tell Joseph not to do?
qa.a: She told him not to send his long reply.

qa.q: What was Joseph feeling as he typed his long reply?
qa.a: He was angry and hurt, and wanted to defend himself against people he felt were lying about him. His shaking hands and hot eyes show it.

qa.q: What steps could Joseph take if the comments continue?
qa.a: He can keep his screenshots as evidence, keep the accounts blocked, avoid replying, and report the abuse to the platform and, if it continues, to a trusted adult or the college.

qa.q: How does Reena see the trolling?
qa.a: Reena sees it as something that says nothing true about Joseph. She helps him step away and studies with him.

grounding: Strangers pile on over a post; the protagonist does not engage, saves evidence, blocks, and leans on a real friend.

subtype: Online group × Being trolled or shamed [Receiver]
passage: Thursday, 1 a.m. Zainab, just breathe. Writing this so I stop reading comments. Yesterday I posted a short video about why our college canteen should have a vegetarian counter and a halal counter side by side. By this evening it had been shared by strangers, and there are over four hundred comments. Some call me names I won't write here. Some say I should be thrown out of college. I typed three long replies and deleted every one. Pradeep came over with instant noodles and sat on the floor with me. He helped me screenshot the worst ones into a folder, then we turned off comments and blocked the accounts that tagged my college. 'These people don't know you,' he said. 'I do.' I'm still shaky. Tomorrow I'll send the folder to the student welfare office.

qa.q: How many comments are on Zainab's video?
qa.a: There are over four hundred comments.

qa.q: What is Zainab feeling while writing at 1 a.m.?
qa.a: Zainab feels shaky, hurt and angry, and is writing just to stop reading the comments.

qa.q: Which steps helped Zainab handle the pile-on?
qa.a: Not replying, saving screenshots as evidence, turning off comments, blocking accounts, and leaning on Pradeep.

qa.q: How does Pradeep see the strangers' comments?
qa.a: Pradeep sees them as coming from people who don't know Zainab, so they say little about who Zainab really is.

grounding: A diary shows strangers piling on over a post, and the wise response of not engaging, saving evidence, blocking and leaning on a real friend.

passage:
Asif: bro did you see what happened to my singing clip
Raghav: saw. some meme page put a clown filter on it
Asif: 2000 comments. people saying my voice should be illegal
Asif: I'm writing a reply to all of them rn
Raghav: don't. that's what they want. they'll screenshot your reply and go again
Asif: so I just take it??
Raghav: you take screenshots. of the page, the comments, the ones using your name. then report + block
Asif: done. 34 screenshots 😔
Raghav: good. now come downstairs. mess has aloo paratha
Asif: not hungry
Raghav: then come sit. these are strangers who laughed for 5 seconds and forgot. your music teacher said you had range. I trust her more than a meme page 🙂
Asif: ok coming

qa.q: How many screenshots did Asif take?
What does Asif's plan to reply to everyone suggest about how Asif feels?
qa.a: It suggests Asif feels humiliated and angry, wanting to fight back against the pile-on.

qa.q: Why was Raghav's advice not to reply wise?
qa.a: Replying would feed the pile-on; saving evidence, reporting, blocking and sitting with a friend protects Asif instead.

qa.q: What would change if Raghav had joined the argument too?
qa.a: The comments would likely have grown, and Asif would have lost the calm friend who pulled Asif away from the screen.

grounding: A chat shows strangers mocking a singing clip, and a friend steering toward not engaging, saving evidence, blocking and real company.
